statement: For three real circles with strictly ordered positive radii in Stoll’s regular nontangent regime, the attainable real solution counts are exactly 0, 4, and 8.

answer.qualification: Generic ordinary-circle regime of Stoll’s classification; special or completed fibres are separate.

source.location: Unnumbered table and following two paragraphs, original p.626; equations (31)–(34), p.625
source.version: Original German journal article (1873), GDZ article scan; PDF page 1 is a digitization cover, original p.613 begins on PDF page 2.

scope: Three ordinary real input circles with strictly ordered positive radii and general centres, excluding mutual tangencies and the collinear-centre/zero-radius/straight-line special loci discussed separately.
notes:
Special tangencies can produce other distinct counts. This is not the spectrum of all singular/completed fibres.

Source discussion. Exactly the generic real counts {0,4,8} occur in the classified cases. The factored pair-discriminants explain why regular counts change in multiples of four.
